verify:c-ports: ics.rs wall_time (SPEC-QUESTION, status item 5): for a UTC time before 1970 the port takes the zone's offset at 1970-01-01T00:00Z. Today's code took the process zone's historical offset at that time. With ChronoZone(Local) in a zone whose offset changed before 1970 (Europe/London 1968–71, say), a timed series anchored before 1970 can land on a different weekday than it does today. Reading A: keep the clamp. Reading B: let a zone answer offsets outside the instant range, e.g. pass the NaiveDateTime through to ChronoZone. Only you can rule on this.
verify:c-ports: weather::build_report sets Report.fetched_at to 0; today's code read SystemTime::now. The caller must fill it in, and device.md should say so wherever it calls build_report.

impl:e1-import: FIXTURE: §15.3 refuses `fixtures/boards/unreadable` and `fixtures/legacy-main/unreadable`, which the brief expected to import. impl:e1-import: SPEC-QUESTION §15.3 step 9.4: 'any `next` that reaches 2^40: fail id_range, listing the ids'. Reading A: fail as soon as next = L+1 equals 2^40, even with nothing to renumber. Reading B: fail only when a renumbering would assign an id of 2^40 or more. I took B: an item at 2^40−1 alone is accepted, with mark 2^40−1.

impl:e1-import: SPEC-QUESTION §15.3 step 9.4: which ids the `id_range` failure lists. Reading A: only the out-of-range ids. Reading B: those plus the old ids that could not be renumbered. I took: the out-of-range ids, ascending and distinct (for id-limits this is exactly the set §18.7 names); when the only cause is next reaching 2^40, the old ids left without a new id (for example [0]).

impl:e1-import: SPEC-QUESTION §15.3 step 12: 'at most 20 subscriptions' is listed among the fields (field_range) and is also a §17 cap (cap). I took field_range, listing the ids past the twentieth. The per-record block caps fail `cap` listing the item or row ids; global caps list no ids.

impl:e1-import: SPEC-QUESTION §15.4: what a failed import's report holds besides the failure (counts so far? warnings from steps 6 and 7?). I took: only `failure`, with every other field at its default. Also, `blocks` counts live blocks only, not archive-row blocks; the spec does not say which.
impl:e1-import: SPEC-QUESTION §15.3 step 11: a leap second (`:60`, which chrono's RFC 3339 parser accepts) is no instant of §5.1. I took `instant_range`.

security:c-ports: Severity: I rated the three resource findings low because common.md calls robustness outside ordinary use low. They are still the serious ones: a 120 KB feed takes 109 s, a 1.1 MB feed takes 178 s, and a 1 MB feed peaks at 1.16 GB. Any URL a user subscribes to can do this to the sync or fetch thread on every refresh. The brief's own property test promises bounded time and does not find these, because random mutations never build long lists.

security:c-ports: core.md §14.6 says the parser is 'today's parser ... everything else is unchanged, including Limits::default()'. That forbids fixing these here. Fixes would need a ruling, for example: cap BYDAY, BYMONTHDAY and BYSETPOS list length and dedup them; cap observances per VTIMEZONE and total transition points, and use binary search in resolve; cap the values per EXDATE or RDATE line; apply the per-event cap after override expansion; use checked add in spread; make the problem line for an undefined TZID not quote the TZID.

security:c-ports: CORE-GEN-010: Parsed.problems and parse's Err quote file text verbatim, with no length limit: the TZID at ics.rs:1283 and the CALSCALE value at ics.rs:515. A quoted TZID may contain anything, a URL included. These strings reach FetchOutcome::Ok.problems and the cache. Does CORE-GEN-010 (no subscription URL or name in any notice or report) cover file text quoted into problems? If yes, both messages need to stop quoting.

security:c-ports: Overlay derives Deserialize, so a device that reads subscribed_cache.json without Overlay::sealed gets unclamped start and end values. With those, minutes(), is_busy() and anchors_on() overflow (a panic in debug). Should the device spec (device.md) require sealed() after reading the cache, as today's read_overlay does?

verify:d-compile: G5 after resolve_on_day is unreachable, because zones never return an out-of-range instant (CORE-TIME-001). Two consequences, both probed: `create` of a task on 9999-12-31 at 1425 in UTC-5 gives core/bad_time with the 'daylight saving' message, not core/date_range; and `create` of an event on 1970-01-01 at 0 in UTC+1 silently steps to 01:00 local (instant 0), where today's code would make 1969-12-31T23:00Z. Should a resolution that falls outside §5.1 be date_range rather than a gap?

verify:d-compile: reflow step 4 against today's code: today moves every flowable whose resolve_on_day(day, m) differs from the stored start, while the spec first skips any flowable with m equal to its current local minutes. The two differ for a block whose stored start has non-zero seconds (today snaps it, the spec leaves it). §13.5 lists only ties as 'changed'. This is harmless if no recorded block carries seconds.

impl:e2-read: Spec question, §18.7 against the brief: §18.7 says the import refuses two of foundation's boards (dst-edges, id-limits), but fixtures/boards/unreadable is refused too: field_range [907], because archive row 907 has a 50,071-byte name, over the 4,096 of §6.6 (it also holds a 70,016-byte line over the line cap). Suggest §18.7 list `unreadable` (field_range) as a third refused board, or say it is to be repaired and compared.

impl:e2-read: SPEC-QUESTION in src/reminders.rs, §14.5: each lead's range is given as 0 to 1,440 minutes, but not what happens to a larger value in `ReminderDefaults`. Reading 1: clamp to 1,440. Reading 2: refuse or treat as invalid. I took reading 1 (clamp).

impl:e2-read: Spec gap, §14.4 (no code comment): `archive_by_day(board, from, days, zone)` allocates one bucket per requested day, so a direct caller passing a huge `days` (e.g. u32::MAX) would try to allocate billions of buckets and abort. `snapshot` clamps to 31 first, so ordinary use is unaffected. Suggest the spec either cap `days` there or leave it to the caller.

security:d-compile: G5 against §5.4 at the edges of the instant range. `create` or `move_block` on 9999-12-31 at 23:45 in UTC−1 answers core/bad_time, because resolve_on_day returns none for an instant out of range; one could read G5 as asking for core/date_range. On 1970-01-01 at 00:00 in UTC+1, resolve_on_day's +60 fallback turns the out-of-range 00:00 local into 01:00 local (1970-01-01T00:00Z), so the item is created an hour later instead of being refused. The spec should say whether an out-of-range local time counts as a gap.
